assistant_message_sections.title: Treat it like an early lung-toxicity signal
assistant_message_sections.content: With a DXd-class ADC, mild exertional dyspnea plus dry cough and SpO2 drift should not be brushed off as simple deconditioning.

assistant_message_sections.title: The next 48 to 72 hours matter most
assistant_message_sections.content: Watch for oxygen falling further, cough worsening, or symptoms shifting from exertional to resting.

assistant_message_sections.title: Save breathing reserve for recovery
assistant_message_sections.content: Lighter meals and slower activity this week can reduce extra respiratory load while the picture becomes clearer.

medication.issues: The bigger issue is not missed medication but quickly identifying whether this is early ADC-related lung toxicity.
medication.adjustments: Keep current medicines steady unless the trial team changes them, but escalate quickly if symptoms worsen before the next dose.

exercise.plan: Use slower, shorter indoor movement and avoid stairs or brisk walking for now.

structured_output.nutrition_advice: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) combine a targeted antibody with a potent cytotoxic payload. While they can attack tumors effectively, off-target effects or payload release may also trigger gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, marrow, or lung toxicity. The core nutrition principles are: higher protein, easy digestion, small frequent meals, and side-effect-specific adjustments. Because ADC targets may be broadly expressed in the gastrointestinal tract, or because the gut lining turns over quickly, nausea, diarrhea, and reduced intake are common. Use small, frequent, bland meals; avoid greasy, fried, and spicy foods; and aim for 5 to 6 eating moments per day without overfilling. Prioritize steamed fish, poached chicken breast, tofu, steamed egg, and vitamin-rich gourd vegetables for higher-protein, easier-to-digest choices. If diarrhea becomes significant, watch for dehydration and electrolyte loss and use oral rehydration solution, or lightly salted rice broth. Avoid milk and dairy because lactose can worsen gut burden. If nausea is severe, avoid large amounts of fluid during meals and move soups and other liquid foods to at least 30 minutes before or after eating. The food goal is lower breathing burden without losing nutrition. Choose warm, easy-to-chew, lower-fat protein options like steamed fish, chicken, tofu, soft noodles, and cooked vegetables, and slow meals down so a full stomach does not worsen breathing.

diet_tips.title: Slow meals down
diet_tips.detail: Talking a lot, eating too fast, or overfilling the stomach can make breathlessness feel worse.

diet_tips.title: Favor warm softer foods
diet_tips.detail: Warm soups, soft porridge, steamed fish, and tofu are easier to finish on a fatigued day.

diet_tips.title: Space fluids through the day
diet_tips.detail: Small frequent drinks are usually more comfortable than trying to catch up all at once.

diet_tips.title: Watch walking tolerance with oxygen
diet_tips.detail: Sometimes walking capacity drops before oxygen numbers look dramatic.

diet_tips.title: Small frequent meals
diet_tips.detail: Aim for 5 to 6 eating moments per day instead of one or two heavy meals to reduce nausea, bloating, and post-meal discomfort.

diet_tips.title: Higher-protein and easy to digest
diet_tips.detail: Steamed fish, poached chicken breast, tofu, and steamed egg are practical ADC-treatment protein staples.

diet_tips.title: Replace fluids and salt during diarrhea
diet_tips.detail: Significant diarrhea causes fluid and electrolyte loss, so use oral rehydration solution or lightly salted rice broth.

diet_tips.title: Pause dairy if diarrhea is active
diet_tips.detail: Lactose in milk and dairy can add to gut burden when diarrhea is already present.

diet_tips.title: Separate larger liquids from meals if nausea is strong
diet_tips.detail: Move soups and other liquid foods to at least 30 minutes before or after eating when nausea is severe.

While they can attack tumors effectively, off-target effects or payload release may also trigger gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, marrow, or lung toxicity. The core nutrition principles are: higher protein, easy digestion, small frequent meals, and side-effect-specific adjustments.
